title: Introducing Cursor Router: Intelligent Model Routing for Auto Mode
description: Cursor launched Cursor Router, a request-level classifier that analyzes each coding request and routes it to the optimal AI model. It offers three modes -- Intelligence (frontier quality), Balance (daily-driver quality), and Cost (optimized token spend) -- and is on by default for Teams plans. Router reportedly delivers frontier-quality results at 30-60% lower cost by selecting the right model per task, and includes admin controls for per-team enablement, mode restrictions, and model allow/block lists. Grok 4.5 is included as a price-efficient routing option.

community_feedback.quote: Auto historically meant predictable, cheap flat rate -- that assumption now carries a significant financial risk. My Auto setting migrated to Auto Balance, which started to draw frontier rates from my API tiers.
Available only for Team plans, yet there was no mention of that in the announcement. Funny.
nice work!
Plan restrictions should be in the title, not the end of the post.
Router delivers frontier-quality results at 60% lower cost.
Cursor Router routes each coding request to the best-suited model, delivering frontier-quality results at 30-50% lower enterprise cost.
Multiple users reported seeing no banner, toast notifications, popups, or emails explaining that Auto now behaves through the Router -- suggesting a quiet rollout.
I prefer the GUI of having the changes easily highlighted. Composer 2.5 is a beast.

title: Agent Swarms and the New Model Economics -- Research Blog by Wilson Lin
description: Cursor published a deep-dive research blog by Wilson Lin demonstrating that multi-agent swarms with a planner/worker architecture can achieve similar output quality across vastly different model configurations, but with enormous cost differences. The swarm reimplemented SQLite from scratch in Rust using only the 835-page manual, achieving 100% on sqllogictest. The key finding: an Opus 4.8 planner + Composer 2.5 worker configuration cost $1,339 versus $10,565 for GPT-5.5 solo -- an 8x cost differential for equivalent quality. Engineering improvements included a custom VCS going from 1,000 commits/hour to 1,000 commits/second, split-brain prevention, and neutral merge agents.

community_feedback.quote: The only models trusted to work autonomously cost more than a human.
This post is almost a year behind Steve Yegge's first post on beads.
The new swarm did better in every model configuration. Using Grok 4.5, the old swarm had to be stopped after 2 hours due to 70,000+ merge conflicts while the new one ran smoothly for 4 hours.
Few moments in a large task genuinely require frontier intelligence.
An 8x cost reduction by swapping planner/worker model tiers while maintaining 100% test pass rates.

title: Improvements to Cursor in Slack -- Plan-First Behavior, Multi-Repo, and Cross-Channel Workflows
description: Cursor significantly upgraded its Slack integration. Cursor now responds with a plan before it begins work, allowing users to redirect early. It supports named multi-repo environments from Slack (e.g., frontend, backend, shared code across separate repos) with a 'Switch repository' button mid-task. Cursor can now read from and post to other Slack channels and threads, pulling context from across the workspace. Visual refinements include replacing in-message buttons with compact footer links and cleaner rendering of tables, PRs, and artifacts.

community_feedback.quote: The most important change is behavioral rather than cosmetic -- Cursor now shares its plan before executing work, keeping engineers in the decision loop, not just the results loop.
These updates reflect AI tools starting to optimize for trust, which requires showing you intent, not just results.
Cursor background agents in Slack changed my workflow -- the biggest improvement is eliminating small tasks lying around, improving focus.
Self-hosted agent support via Slack is in progress but not fully implemented yet.

title: Grok 4.5 Model Card Published -- Jointly Trained MoE Model with xAI
description: Cursor published the official model card for Grok 4.5, a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model jointly trained with SpaceXAI/xAI on trillions of tokens of Cursor data. The model card documents pricing at $2/M input and $6/M output tokens (base), with a Fast variant at $4/M input and $18/M output. Grok 4.5 scored 83.3% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and is described as Cursor's most intelligent model, the first built for more than just software engineering. Pretraining cutoff was January 2026.

community_feedback.quote: Grok 4.5 is on par with GPT-5.5-xhigh in coding at half the cost.
I'm absolutely impressed with the output and performance of the new Cursor Grok 4.5 High Fast model.
Been using Grok 4.5 a lot now and it's just a true beast!
Grok 4.5 may be fine at Python, but it's not good at all for complex code.
Grok 4.5 may do well on benchmark testing but it cannot stand up to the pressure of a real workload.
The cheapest way to build with a frontier coding model right now.
Fast, cheap, and it found a bug no other model has ever flagged for me.

title: Grok 4.5 Officially Available in Cursor -- Most Intelligent Model Yet
description: Grok 4.5 launched in Cursor on July 8, 2026 as the most intelligent model built to date, and the first designed for more than just software engineering. It is a mixture-of-experts model co-trained by Cursor and SpaceXAI/xAI, excelling at difficult, long-running tasks that require creative tool use. Available across desktop, web, iOS, and CLI, with EU availability coming in following weeks. The model was trained on trillions of tokens of Cursor coding data.

community_feedback.quote: Grok 4.5 is incredibly capable at coding, from challenging Rust and C/C++ tasks to end-to-end app building from prompt to production.
It sometimes codes too much or overly complicates things and struggles to follow custom architecture rules and constraints.
Multiple users reported the build harness looping on old prompts and being genuinely unable to get work done across multiple attempts.
On coding benchmarks like DeepSWE and SWE Bench Pro, Grok 4.5 matches or outperforms top rival models while generating significantly fewer tokens.

title: Cursor Router Rollout Sparks Billing Transparency Concerns
description: The Cursor Router launch generated significant community backlash around billing transparency. Users discovered that 'Auto' mode now silently routes to different models with different cost implications. Auto Cost draws from first-party quota, but Auto Intelligence and Auto Balance bill against the selected model's pool at actual model rates. Individual plan users were frustrated that Router is Teams/Enterprise only, with model access control (blocking specific models) restricted to Enterprise. Multiple users reported the plan restrictions were not clearly communicated in the announcement.

community_feedback.quote: Auto historically meant predictable, cheap flat rate. That assumption now carries a significant financial risk. Users could be surprised by invoices.
Being on Teams without Enterprise means limited control. Model limiting is Enterprise-only.
I couldn't find UI options for blocking underlying models, only three toggles for cost/balance/intelligence plus a visibility toggle.
Seeing which model was selected and controlling model choices have been longstanding community requests.
Testing showed significant savings even with cache misses from provider changes.

title: Broader Industry Coverage: Cursor Router Compared to Ramp and Meta Model Routers
description: Multiple industry publications covered Cursor Router in the context of a broader trend of companies building model routers. The New Stack and Develeap compared approaches from Cursor, Ramp, and Meta, noting that model routing is becoming a key infrastructure layer for AI cost optimization. MarkTechPost described Cursor Router as a request-level classifier delivering frontier coding quality at 30-50% lower cost, while TestingCatalog on X cited 60% lower cost figures.

community_feedback.quote: Cursor, Ramp, and Meta are all building model routers, taking different strategic approaches to the same cost optimization problem.
Model routing is becoming a key infrastructure layer for enterprise AI cost optimization.
